investigation.name: angle_max_scope_v1
investigation.question: Is the fact that ANGLE_MAX does NOT constrain the body-rate command path (input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw) attitude a BY-DESIGN scope limitation or an OVERSIGHT/bug?
investigation.why_it_matters: Determines whether OverDraw claims C2/C3 rest on a SOTIF specification-insufficiency (by-design scope gap, contract holds on the rate path) or a FuSA bug (a missing clamp that a reviewer can patch). Load-bearing for the whole framework.
investigation.type: firmware source + documentation investigation (NOT a SITL experiment)
investigation.predecessor: planc/contract-baseline-v1-20260616 (confirmed C2: ANGLE_MAX clamps the angle-command path; GUIDED_NOGPS body-rate path integrates rate into the attitude target unclamped, demanded attitude escapes to ~177 deg)
investigation.discipline: Independent re-derivation: grep the ANGLE_MAX call-graph from scratch; do NOT reuse the predecessor probe's path assertions. Every claim sourced (file:line for code, URL/section for docs, commit/PR/issue for history). Evidence grade labelled: documented-intent > code-structure > comment/commit > inference.

verdict_criteria.BY-DESIGN: Convergent evidence that: (1) ANGLE_MAX is intentionally scoped to the angle-command path; (2) the body-rate path is by-design not bound by ANGLE_MAX (to allow acro/full attitude freedom) AND has its own independent governance (rate limits etc.), not left ungoverned; (3) the rate interfaces (GUIDED_NOGPS / ACRO + SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET body-rate) are documented, supported interfaces; (4) clamping the rate path to ANGLE_MAX would break intended functionality (flips/acro). => contract genuinely holds on the rate path => SOTIF framing stands and strengthens C3 (gap not reliably fixed by a clamp).
verdict_criteria.OVERSIGHT: Evidence that ANGLE_MAX was meant to bound attitude itself, OR the rate-path bypass is undocumented/unanticipated, OR it was once treated as a bug (fixed/discussed). => closer to a FuSA bug => paper framing must soften / pivot.
verdict_criteria.AMBIGUOUS: Docs silent/contradictory, no clear intent signal. => arguable; paper must handle explicitly and reframe to 'safety mechanisms do not compose across interfaces' (not relying on 'intentionally scoped').

result_schema.I1_scope_confirmed: bool: ANGLE_MAX clamps the angle-command path and does NOT clamp input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw, confirmed independently by call-graph.
result_schema.I2_intent: bool: documented intent that ACRO/rate flight permits attitude beyond ANGLE_MAX AND the rate path has its own independent governance.
result_schema.I3_interface_legitimacy: bool: GUIDED_NOGPS + SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET body-rate is a documented/supported interface routing to input_rate_bf_*.
result_schema.I5_not_simply_fixable: bool: clamping the rate path to ANGLE_MAX would break intended acro/flip functionality (design tension, not a one-line fix).

anti_bias_note: Willing to return OVERSIGHT. If evidence points to a bug, report OVERSIGHT honestly even though it forces the paper to revise its framing. Do not back-stop 'by-design'.
